decision: Retain clearer publication-policy ownership and shared commit phases without result-object allocation or a forwarding-only coordinator. This is an architectural simplification, not a speedup claim.

environment.gc: enabled; collected before each measured batch
environment.io: warm OS page cache; no fsync; final buffer drain included
environment.memory: fresh-process Linux RSS, including native allocations

environment.gc: enabled; collected before each measured batch
environment.io: warm OS page cache; no fsync; final buffer drain included
environment.memory: fresh-process Linux RSS, including native allocations

regressions: Summary hook installed during flush receives the same commit
Summary replacement during flush is resolved dynamically
Commit callback replacement during flush is not bypassed
History reinitialization clears publication capability registration

limitations: Hundred-metric means vary from -0.77% to +1.96%; no speedup claim.
Five-metric mean overhead is +1.97% and +2.77% in independent confirmation (~0.33 us/log).
NumPy p99 rises from 89.00 to 103.57 us; tail latency is not uniformly preserved.
Reader-contention mean changes +4.18% then -1.24%; high variation prevents a precise attribution.
Callback/provider references can still retain Run; removal of a dedicated back-reference does not remove all object-reference cycles.
Cross-language transaction stages, compatibility hooks and Python SDK remain.
Intermediate wrapper/forwarding versions are not the final implementation and their campaigns are not included as final performance evidence.
